socfpga_gic_reg.h

GIC register definition header for the SoCFPGA bare-metal software stack.

gic_reg_enable_group0_interrupts
void gic_reg_enable_group0_interrupts(
void
)

Enables the signaling of Group 0 interrupts to the executing Processing Element (PE).

In the ARM GIC architecture, Group 0 interrupts are typically reserved for Secure interrupts and are signaled as FIQs. This function performs a direct write to the `ICC_IGRPEN0_EL1` system register to assert the enable bit, allowing the CPU interface to forward pending Group 0 interrupts to the core.

Returns

None.

gic_reg_enable_group1_interrupts
void gic_reg_enable_group1_interrupts(
void
)

Enables the signaling of Group 1 interrupts to the executing Processing Element (PE).

Group 1 interrupts are typically used for Non-Secure general-purpose interrupts (signaled as IRQs). This function writes to the `ICC_IGRPEN1_EL1` system register to unmask Group 1 delivery at the CPU interface level.

Returns

None.

gic_reg_write_group1_end_of_interrupt
void gic_reg_write_group1_end_of_interrupt(
uint32_t 
interrupt_id
)

Signals the completion of the active Group 1 interrupt handling routine.

This function writes the specified interrupt ID to the End of Interrupt (EOI) register (`ICC_EOIR1_EL1`). This critical action informs the GIC hardware that the processor has finished servicing the interrupt, causing the GIC to perform a priority drop and transition the interrupt state from Active to Inactive (or Pending if another edge was detected).

Parameters
interrupt_id
uint32_t

The hardware INTID of the serviced interrupt (read previously from the Interrupt Acknowledge Register, `ICC_IAR1_EL1`).

Returns

None.

gic_reg_set_priority_mask
void gic_reg_set_priority_mask(
uint32_t 
priority_mask
)

Sets the priority threshold for forwarding interrupts to the CPU.

This function writes directly to the Priority Mask Register (`ICC_PMR_EL1`).  The GIC CPU interface will only signal pending interrupts that have a higher priority (a strictly lower value) than this mask. Setting this to 0xFF effectively allows all configured interrupts to be serviced.

Parameters
priority_mask
uint32_t

The 8-bit priority threshold value.

Returns

None.

gic_reg_get_cpu_affinity
uint64_t gic_reg_get_cpu_affinity(
void
)

Retrieves the hardware routing identification for the currently executing core.

This function reads the Multiprocessor Affinity Register (`MPIDR_EL1`) to extract the Aff0, Aff1, Aff2, and Aff3 fields. These hierarchical affinity levels are used by the GICv3 distributor (via the `IROUTER` registers) to route specific Shared Peripheral Interrupts (SPIs) to this exact CPU core.

Returns

The 64-bit affinity descriptor containing the hierarchical cluster and core IDs.
